Is the Hessian Positive Definite?

Source: R/mxHelper-has-pd-hessian.R
MxHelperHasPdHessian.Rd

Tests whether the Hessian of a fitted model is positive definite: its smallest eigenvalue exceeds \(\tau_{\mathrm{abs}} + \tau_{\mathrm{rel}} \max \left( 1, \max_{i} \left| \lambda_{i} \right| \right)\). With check_condition = TRUE, its condition number must also be at most cond_max. A missing Hessian counts as not positive definite. The arguments are checked first; the internal version, without checks, is the one other projects copy.

Usage

MxHelperHasPdHessian(
  x,
  hess_tol_abs = 1e-08,
  hess_tol_rel = 1e-10,
  check_condition = FALSE,
  cond_max = 1e+12
)

Arguments

x

An OpenMx model (MxModel), usually fitted.

hess_tol_abs

Positive number. Absolute tolerance on the smallest eigenvalue of the Hessian.

hess_tol_rel

Positive number. Tolerance on the smallest eigenvalue of the Hessian, relative to its largest absolute eigenvalue.

check_condition

Logical. If TRUE, the Hessian must also have a condition number of at most cond_max.

cond_max

Positive number. Largest condition number of the Hessian.

Value

Returns TRUE or FALSE.

See also

Other Fit Diagnostics Functions: MxHelperIsGoodFit(), MxHelperNeedsRescue(), MxHelperStatusCode()

Author

Ivan Jacob Agaloos Pesigan

Examples

set.seed(seed = 42)
x <- data.frame(
  y1 = rnorm(n = 50),
  y2 = rnorm(n = 50)
)
fit <- MxHelperQuiet(
  expr = MxHelperMuSigma(
    x = x,
    extraTries = 2
  )
)
MxHelperHasPdHessian(
  x = fit
)
#> [1] TRUE
